source: Written by the Interim team after the 2026-10-11 playtest (CONTRACTS.md R5.3). Both texts are SYNTHETIC; no real patient is described. N-HYPO is a realistic oncology clinic note in the style of the 8 chart notes of chartscan_answer_key.json; C-STOOLS is the playtest coordinator's phone-call summary word for word.
rationale: A small, honest key for the second reader (Gemini): the deterministic scanner is scored on 43 cases in chartscan_answer_key.json and stays at 100% without any model. This key asks the narrower question the model exists for, 'what does the reader add that the scanner misses, and does it add anything wrong?'. N-HYPO holds a finding outside the scanner's lexicon (hypothyroidism, an immune-related endocrine event) next to negations ('Denies diarrhea ...') the reader must not turn into side effects. C-STOOLS is the case where the scanner was wrong (graded 1 instead of 3, fixed by the stool-count pattern) and the reader must agree with the corrected rule. scripts/eval_reader.py runs both sides over this key from the recorded cache (no network) and writes docs/eval/reader_results.md. Two cases are a smoke test, not an accuracy estimate: the report says so.

cases.author: J. Rivera, NP
cases.text: Oncology clinic follow-up, cycle 6 of cemiplimab. Pt reports feeling more tired than usual for about 3 weeks, with cold intolerance and dry skin. Denies diarrhea, shortness of breath, or rash. No fever. Labs today: TSH 18.2 (H), free T4 0.6 (L). Hypothyroidism, grade 2, likely immune-related. Started levothyroxine 50 mcg daily. Will recheck TSH in 6 weeks. Continue cemiplimab per protocol.
